extracted.intended_audience: general readers, students, journalists, and human-rights researchers/advocates interested in Benin
extracted.subtask_description: Country-level overview of the human-rights situation in Benin covering legal guarantees, enforcement, sectoral rights (women, children, disabled, LGBT), institutional frameworks, international commitments, and historical ratings. It summarizes problems (e.g., prison conditions, police abuse, child labor) and reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: International human-rights treaties and commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Benin is a signatory of the following international agreements: African (Banjul) Charter on Human and People's Rights; Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhumane, or Degrading Treatment or Punishment; Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women; Convention on the Rights of the Child; International Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination; International Covenant Economic, Social and Cultural Rights; and International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing membership/ratification of international instruments is used to assess the country's formal legal obligations and commitments. The article cites these treaties as a basis for evaluating whether Benin's domestic laws and practices align with international norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom House political rights and civil liberties ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: A Freedom in the World chart of Benin's ratings since 1972 in the Freedom House reports; 'A rating of 1 is "free"; 7, "not free".' The table shows year-by-year political rights and civil liberties scores and status (Free/Partly Free/Not Free).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical numeric ratings (political rights, civil liberties) are presented as a standard metric for tracking changes over time and for cross-country comparison. The chart provides context for assessing trends in Benin's democratic and human-rights performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional guarantees vs practice (legal protections exist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benin's constitution and laws guarantee freedom of speech, of the press, freedom of assembly, movement, religious freedom, and prohibit discrimination based on race, gender, disability, language, and social status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of constitutional or statutory guarantees is a baseline criterion; the article repeatedly contrasts these formal guarantees with weaknesses in implementation and enforcement, implying an assessment should measure both legal text and actual practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of expression and press freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Benin's constitution and laws guarantee freedom of speech and of the press, these rights are sometimes denied. Government broadcasting office (ORTB) has restricted critical broadcasts; government blocked a French radio signal in 2010 and allegedly purchased large numbers of newspapers reporting on corruption. Many journalists engage in self-censorship; some have been sued for libel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate both formal protections and concrete acts (broadcast blocks, censorship, libel suits, self-censorship, government ownership/aid to media). Consider reach of media and literacy limitations when assessing real-world access to information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of assembly and association
rubrics_metrics.description: The government generally respects the right to freedom of assembly but sometimes refuses permits for opposition groups and others; in 2010 the government prohibited several public gatherings including union demonstrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should look at permit issuance practices, instances of bans, treatment of peaceful demonstrations, and restrictions tied to political opposition or labor activity (notice requirements, prohibitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to movement and travel
rubrics_metrics.description: Benin's constitution and laws guarantee the right to move freely around the country, travel abroad, emigrate and repatriate, and these rights are generally honored, although checkpoints around the country are used by police and gendarmes to demand bribes. Minors require documentation when traveling abroad to avoid trafficking; uneven enforcement contributes to trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure both legal guarantees and on-the-ground practices such as checkpoints, bribery, and enforcement gaps that affect mobility and contribute to trafficking risks for minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Benin is a secular state in which religious freedom is guaranteed to all and public schools are not permitted to give religious instruction (private religious schools are permitted). Respect for religious differences is widespread, though occasional conflicts (e.g., between Voodoo practitioners and Christians) occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess formal secularism and protections, prevalence of inter-religious respect, and any incidents of conflict or state interference in religious practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-discrimination protections and their effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination based on race, gender, disability, language, and social status is prohibited by the constitution and laws; however, women and disabled people continue to experience discrimination, and the government does little to combat it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for statutory prohibitions and enforcement mechanisms, prevalence of discrimination in practice, and government action (or inaction) to address discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corruption and anti-corruption institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Corruption exists in virtually all sectors and levels of government in Benin. There is a government agency called the Watchdog to Combat Corruption, whose ostensible purpose is to address this problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider prevalence of corrupt practices (e.g., bribery at checkpoints), effectiveness and independence of anti-corruption bodies, and evidence of enforcement or political will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women's rights and gender equality (laws vs enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Women's rights have improved since restoration of democracy and passage of the Personal and Family Code in 2004, but inequality and discrimination persist. Polygamy and forced marriage are illegal but still occur. Enforcement of rape laws is hampered by corruption, ineffective police work, and fear of stigma. Domestic violence is widespread. Female genital mutilation (FGM) affects about 13% overall (higher in some regions) and laws against it are rarely enforced. Women face sexual harassment, limited access to credit, and problems managing property when widowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legal reforms alongside enforcement, social norms, prevalence of practices (FGM, child/forced marriage), access to services and remedies, and existence/availability of NGOs and support services for victims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's rights (birth registration, protection, trafficking and labor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many births are unrecorded, causing denial of education and health care. Primary school is compulsory but many girls do not attend. Child marriage is widespread despite legal limits. Practices such as infanticide of 'abnormal' newborns and 'vidomègon' (placing poor children as domestic servants) occur, resulting in exploitation and trafficking. Child prostitution and child labor are problems. The Minors Protection Brigade exists to act when children are in moral or physical danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate registration systems, enforcement of child-protection laws, prevalence of harmful customs, child-labor enforcement, availability of juvenile justice, and protective agencies' capacity and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disabled persons' rights and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no law banning discrimination against disabled individuals and no law requiring buildings to be wheelchair-accessible. Little institutional help exists and disabled people generally support themselves through begging. Protections in labor law for disabled workers exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legal protections specifically addressing disability discrimination and accessibility, availability of social/institutional support, and enforcement of any labor protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBT rights and decriminalization of same-sex relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Benin rejected a recommendation to 'decriminalize sexual relations between consenting, same-sex individuals' and the U.S. reported continued concern about LGBT citizens, calling for decriminalization and educational/police policies that promote personal security regardless of sexual orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider criminalization status, government responses to international recommendations, protections from discrimination or violence, and whether educational/police training/programs exist to safeguard LGBT persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV/AIDS-related non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: It is illegal to discriminate against people based on HIV status, and overt instances of such discrimination are reportedly not frequent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess existence of legal protections, frequency of reported discriminatory incidents, and access to health services and social support for people living with HIV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minority ethnic representation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no majority ethnic group in Benin. A range of ethnic groups is represented in the public sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate political and administrative representation, inclusion in public services, and whether minority groups face systemic exclusion or discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refugee and asylum-seeker protections
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a system for protecting refugees; the country held about 7,300 refugees at the end of 2010, most from Togo. Benin works with UNHCR and other groups to assist such individuals. Those who do not qualify as refugees are invited to apply for residence permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legal framework for refugee status determination, cooperation with UNHCR, availability of protection and assistance, and pathways for non-refugee migrants to obtain legal residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees' rights, collective bargaining and strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Workers are allowed to unionize and to strike, although they must provide three days' notice and the government can prohibit strikes for various reasons. Workers (except merchant shipping) are entitled to bargain collectively. Forced labor is illegal but exists. Child labor restrictions exist (under-12 prohibition, 12–14 light work permitted) but are poorly enforced. Labor code enforcement is weak, minimum wage is very low, and health and safety standards are not effectively enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess statutory labor rights (unionization, strike rules, collective bargaining), notice and restriction mechanisms, enforcement capacity (inspectors), prevalence of forced/child labor, and labor-market protections in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrest, detention and treatment of persons under arrest
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitrary arrest is illegal, but it occurs. Under the constitution, defendants cannot be arrested without warrants and evidence and must be arraigned by a judge within 48 hours, but these rules are not always observed. Police and gendarmes are ill-equipped and ill-trained. Torture is banned but does occur; detainees are often beaten and a 2010 death in custody (Adam Yessoufa) was reported after a beating by security forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate compliance with arrest/warrant procedures, timeliness of arraignment, access to counsel, training and equipment of security forces, prevalence of torture/beatings, and accountability for abuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial process and trial rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials are often delayed due to overcrowded dockets and inadequate staff and facilities. Although the judiciary is supposed to be independent, it is susceptible to influence by other branches of government and there is widespread corruption. Defendants have rights under French civil law (jury trial, presumption of innocence, right to attorney, to confront witnesses, to appeal) and these rights are generally respected. Young defendants are not tried in juvenile courts, representing a violation of international norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess judicial independence, case-backlog and resources, observance of fair-trial rights, corruption in the judiciary, and existence and functioning of juvenile justice mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison conditions and treatment of inmates
rubrics_metrics.description: Prisons are overcrowded (one prison housed six times official capacity). Problems include malnutrition, disease, poor sanitation, inadequate medical care, and lack of ventilation. Juveniles are often imprisoned with adults. Women are often imprisoned with their children and give birth in prison without a doctor present. Human-rights monitors are allowed to visit. Calls exist to improve conditions and reduce pre-trial detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate overcrowding rates, health and sanitary conditions, separation of juveniles, medical care availability, treatment of pregnant women and children in prison, access for monitors, and measures to reduce pre-trial detention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital punishment status
rubrics_metrics.description: Capital punishment is still officially legal in Benin, and convicts are still sentenced to death, but no executions have taken place since 1987.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between legal status (retentionist) and practice (de facto moratorium). Assess sentencing trends and any moves toward abolition or formal moratorium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the internet and information infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an unrestricted right of access to the Internet, but it is unavailable in most places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess legal protections for internet access, actual coverage and availability, and the role of connectivity in enabling freedom of expression and access to information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to strike and anti-union governmental behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Report expresses concern about serious restrictions on the right to strike in the public sector and authorities' frequent anti-union statements, fueling social tensions and protest actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate specific restrictions on strikes (notice periods, grounds for prohibition), government rhetoric/actions toward unions, and the impact on labor rights and social stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and role of national human-rights institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. report applauded 'the establishment of human rights institutions including the human rights Ombudsman and the National Council for the Promotion of Gender Equity and Equality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence, mandate, independence, resources, and effectiveness of national human-rights institutions in protecting rights and holding authorities accountable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap between laws on the books and enforcement in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated theme: laws exist protecting various rights (e.g., against discrimination, rape penalties, child labor restrictions) but enforcement is weak due to corruption, ineffective police work, lack of inspectors, and social stigma. Examples include rare prosecution of FGM, reduced prosecution of sexual offenses to misdemeanors, and poor enforcement of labor laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive assessment should measure both the existence of legal/regulatory frameworks and the capacity, will, and mechanisms for enforcement; note causes of enforcement gaps (corruption, resources, customs, stigma).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mob justice and community violence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a problem with acts of violence committed by mobs against suspected criminals whom they feel have been inadequately punished by the courts; members of such mobs are often not arrested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prevalence of mob violence, reasons behind it (perceived impunity), law-enforcement responses, and community-level conflict-resolution mechanisms.
